conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: COBOL character repertoire (if more than one encoding in a compilation group, control functions if any)
rows.adjudicator-notes: Optional facility PROVIDED, so the row is 'Provided' (not the PB280 Q1 'Not provided.' form). Verified: CompilationInputs.ReadAllText = File.ReadAllText (BOM detection, UTF-8 default), called for the source (Frontend.cs:126) and every copybook (CopyProcessor.cs:430). Probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s1/probe/i26.cob (UTF-8, no BOM) COPYing c16.cpy (UTF-16LE+BOM, VALUE "O€K"), c32.cpy (UTF-32LE+BOM), c16be.cpy (UTF-16BE+BOM), c8b.cpy (UTF-8+BOM), plus its own UTF-8 é€! literal -> 'O€K|OK|OK|OK|é€!' at --std 2023. Refuter probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s1/refute-probe/r26.cob (UTF-8+BOM main COPYing b32.cpy UTF-32BE+BOM 'O€K' and b16.cpy UTF-16LE+BOM 'AéB', --copy .) -> 'O€K|AéB|3' at --std 85 and 2023, so UTF-32 big-endian and a BOM on the main source are verified too. The row deliberately does not describe malformed-byte handling — that is the item-25 defect (U+FFFD substitution, proposed new note). No spec-derived pin (—). cite.py --check 8.1.3.2 'If more than one encoding is permitted in a single compilation group, the implementor shall specify the control functions or other methods used for distinguishing between encodings' OK (2). Owning note: PB1397 (open; claims DOC-A.1-26).
rows.rule-text: COBOL character repertoire (if more than one encoding in a compilation group, control functions if any). Multiple encodings are optional and control functions are optional. This item is conditionally required because it is conditioned upon support of multiple encodings in a compilation group where control functions are defined for switching between encodings. This item, if provided by the implementor, shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (8.1.3, COBOL character repertoire)

rows.subject: COBOL words
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: `OK  §8.3.2.1 4)` "A given word may be used as a system-name and as a user-defined word, subject to the rules specified in 8.3.2.2, User-defined words, and 8.3.2.3, System-names." System-names are held apart from user-defined words by construction: implementor names live in the ONE table ImplementorNames (a SPECIAL-NAMES entry's system-name position), computer-names are read by text in the configuration paragraphs, and none of them is entered into the data-name / procedure-name / mnemonic namespaces, so a data-name, paragraph-name or mnemonic-name spelled like a system-name never collides. PROBE (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/sysuser/su1.cob) at 85 and 2023: SOURCE-COMPUTER. MYBOX. + 01 MYBOX (computer-name = data-name), CONSOLE IS CONSOLE (device-name = its own mnemonic-name), SYSOUT IS OUTDEV + 01 SYSOUT (device-name = data-name), SWITCH-1 IS SW1 + 01 SWITCH-1 (switch-name = data-name), 01 C01 (feature-name = data-name), paragraph SYSERR (device-name = paragraph-name) -> compiles and prints MSWC / K at both editions (DISPLAY UPON OUTDEV and UPON CONSOLE route to the device, the data-names read their own values). The 'subject to 8.3.2.3' half: §8.3.2.3.1's one-type rule for device/feature/switch names holds by construction — ImplementorName carries exactly ONE SystemNameKind per name (ImplementorNamesDriftTests). The 'subject to 8.3.2.2' half defers to §8.3.2.2's own rows; its one-type-of-user-defined-word restriction is unenforced and owned by open kb/Work PB990 (rows SR-8.3.2.2-1/-2/-3), which concerns two USER-DEFINED types and not the system-name/user-word sharing this row permits. No spec-derived test names this row (the dossier's §8.3.2.1 test citations are all rule 1 / rule 3 / rule 5 / word length), so test-ref is empty. || editions as written by the adjudicator: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the permission is unchanged across editions; the §8.3.2.3 system-name types it references grew — call-convention-name, entry-convention-name, external-locale-name — but the sharing permission applies to whichever types an edition has)
rows.rule-text: A given word may be used as a system-name and as a user-defined word, subject to the rules specified in 8.3.2.2, User-defined words, and 8.3.2.3, System-names.

rows.subject: COBOL words
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: `OK  §8.3.2.2 2)` "a level-number may be the same as a paragraph-name or a section-name". Level-numbers are INTEGERLIT tokens in the data description entry and never enter the procedure table, while all-digit paragraph and section names are admitted by the procedureName definition slot. PROBES (pinned cobol.exe, out/probe/onetype): ex2.cob — paragraphs 01, 05 and 88 beside 01/05-level data, PERFORM 05 / PERFORM 88 -> `05 RAN 7` / `88 RAN` at 85 and 2023; ex2b.cob — `77 SECTION.`, paragraph `01.`, `05 SECTION.` containing paragraph `77.`, beside 77 N and 01 G / 05 X, with PERFORM 05 and GO TO 88 -> `05S 71` / `END` at 85 and 2023. The exception's complement (a level-number spelled like any OTHER type) is unreachable: every other type must contain a letter (§8.3.2.2) and an all-digit word lexes INTEGERLIT, so no other declaration slot can take it. REGISTER: open kb/Work PB990 lists this row in inventory_rows because its one-type census must carry this exception as data (keep it when the census lands). No spec-derived test names the exception; test-ref empty.
rows.rule-text: a level-number may be the same as a paragraph-name or a section-name

rows.subject: COBOL-WORDS directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR1 'The content of each literal shall be processed as case-insensitive ... Any use of an equated or substituted literal shall be case-insensitive when used syntactically as a COBOL word' (cite.py OK §7.3.10.4 1)). Literal() upper-cases the content (ToUpperInvariant); CobolWordsMap dictionaries/sets are OrdinalIgnoreCase; the rewriter's synonym lookup is OrdinalIgnoreCase. Probe case_insens: EQUATE "display" WITH "show" then 'Show "OK-CASE"' and 'sHoW "OK-CASE2"' both DISPLAY (both halves verified by probe). unit:CobolWordsDirectiveTests.Literals_AreCaseInsensitive covers only the literal-content half (not the use-in-source half), so no test-ref is claimed: test-needed for the second half. || editions (adjudicator): 2023 only (new in COBOL-2023: Foreword list 'Additional compiler directives were added: COBOL-WORDS directive'; Annex E.3.3 item 12, cite.py OK §E.3.3 12)); below 2023 the directive word is COBOLNET0900 || code-location not resolvable in the tree (registrar 15a): src/Cobol.Net.Editions/CobolWordsMap.cs#CobolWordsMap..ctor
rows.rule-text: The content of each literal shall be processed as case-insensitive whenever the COBOL-WORDS directive is applied within a compilation group. Any use of an equated or substituted literal shall be case-insensitive when used syntactically as a COBOL word.

rows.subject: COBOL-WORDS directive
rows.adjudicator-notes: GR6 'A COBOL-WORDS directive does not affect any Compiler directing statements or Compiler directives' (cite.py OK §7.3.10.4 6)). Structural: the map is built from the FINAL preprocessed text (after COPY/REPLACE and directive processing) and applied only by the post-lex token rewriter and binder, so text-manipulation constructs never see it. Probed: UNDEFINE "COPY" then COPY CWBOOK still copies; SUBSTITUTE "REPLACE" BY "SWAPIT" -> REPLACE still works and REPLACE usable as data-name; EQUATE "REPLACE" WITH "SWAPIT" -> SWAPIT ==A== BY ==B== is NOT a REPLACE (rejected); SUBSTITUTE "IF" BY "WHENIF" -> >>IF/>>END-IF still work while the IF statement is WHENIF; UNDEFINE "SOURCE" -> >>SOURCE FORMAT FREE still works. No spec-derived test pins GR6: test-needed. || editions (adjudicator): 2023 only (new in COBOL-2023: Foreword list 'Additional compiler directives were added: COBOL-WORDS directive'; Annex E.3.3 item 12, cite.py OK §E.3.3 12)); below 2023 the directive word is COBOLNET0900
rows.rule-text: A COBOL-WORDS directive does not affect any Compiler directing statements or Compiler directives.

rows.subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.7.3 "Record-key-name-1 shall be a name specified as a record-key-name" OK. ResolveFileCollating builds keyNames from RecordKeyName + AlternateKeyNames and refuses any Format-2 name outside it (COBOLNET1582, 'SR4/SR5'). record-key-name-1 can only be defined by the `record-key-name-1 SOURCE IS` key form, which CONFORMANCE.md row 40 declares Not claimed and DataBinder.DeclineRecordKeySource refuses by name (COBOLNET1954) at every edition — so no accepted program can hold a record-key-name, and every Format-2 name that is not a declared key's data-name is refused. The SR5 arm is therefore enforced (vacuously) for all accepted source; no open note needed (row 40's witnesses are PB358, landed). FileCollatingSequenceSpecTests.KeyLevel_NameThatIsNotAKey_Diagnosed covers SR4's data-name arm, not SR5 — test-ref left empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85: the file-control COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is a 2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 delta for it)]
rows.rule-text: Record-key-name-1 shall be a name specified as a record-key-name in an ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause or in a RECORD KEY clause in the file control entry.

rows.subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.7.3 "Data-name-1 and record-key-name-1 shall not be subscripted" OK. Format 2's operand is `cobolWord+`, which cannot carry a subscript: probe p11 `COLLATING SEQUENCE OF IX-KEY(1) IS REV` -> `COBOL0312: unexpected '('` (a generic parse error rather than a named SR6 diagnostic, but the source is rejected at every edition). No spec-derived test. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85: the file-control COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is a 2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 delta for it)]
rows.rule-text: Data-name-1 and record-key-name-1 shall not be subscripted.

rows.subject: COLLATING SEQUENCE clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.4.5.7.4 "the native alphanumeric collating sequence applies to any record keys of class alphanumeric" OK. When alphabet-name-1 is absent and no key-level clause names the key, `alphabet` stays null -> native ordinal (null weights). Probe p2 (only FOR NATIONAL written): the alphanumeric alternate key IX-ALT read A,M,Z (native); probe p5 (key-level on the prime only): IX-ALT A,M,Z native. No-clause files take the early return to native. No spec-derived test isolates this rule. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (absent from COBOL-85: the file-control COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is a 2002 introduction; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 delta for it)]
rows.rule-text: If alphabet-name-1 is not specified in the file control entry, the native alphanumeric collating sequence applies to any record keys of class alphanumeric, whether primary or alternate, not specified in a key-level format of another COLLATING SEQUENCE clause.

rows.subject: COLUMN clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.18.14.3 "COLUMN, COL, COLUMNS, and COLS are synonyms." -> OK SR1. The report production takes all four spellings in one alternative and the binder reads only the operands (reportColumnOperand), so the spelling cannot change the meaning. Probes at 2023 (out13/probe/column-clause-p1/syn_col, syn_cols, syn_columns, syn_colnumis): `COL 5`, `COLS 5`, `COLUMNS 5`, `COL NUMBER IS 5` each print 'A' in column 5, identical to `COLUMN 5`. At --std 85 `COL 5` is refused COBOLNET0900 (the non-COLUMN spellings are 2002 introductions — gate in VisitReportColumnClause; edition edge derived, not quoted). Format 2 half: the screen module is declined (A.4.2 Not claimed, PB260 owns it). Test-needed: conformance:2023/pb506_report_value_operand_list and 2002/pb506_report_operand_lists_2002 exercise COLUMNS ARE only (derived for §13.18.63.3 SR35, not SR1); no spec-derived test witnesses COL/COLS equivalence. || Editions (adjudicator): 85 (single absolute COLUMN NUMBER IS integer-1 form), 2002, 2014, 2023 — Report Writer is in every edition; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change to §13.18.14; the COL/COLS/COLUMNS/NUMBERS/ARE/multiple/relative forms are 2002 introductions (derived, repo holds no 85/2002 text)
rows.rule-text: COLUMN, COL, COLUMNS, and COLS are synonyms.

rows.subject: COLUMN clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'The COLUMN clause defines one or more printable items. If a COLUMN clause is not specified, the items are not printed.' (cite.py --check 13.18.14.4 -> OK §13.18.14.4 1)). Only entries with a COLUMN clause become ReportFieldModel placements; the compose method places only those. Probe p1.cob (2002): a `03 PIC 999 SOURCE WS-X.` entry with no COLUMN on a line alongside `COLUMN PLUS 3 PIC XX VALUE "QQ"` printed only '  QQ' (the SOURCE item not printed, and QQ is the line's first printable item at column 3). The VALUE-without-COLUMN shape is separately refused per §13.15.3 SR13 (conformance:negative/pb853-report-value-without-column). No spec-derived golden pins the not-printed half; test-needed.
rows.rule-text: The COLUMN clause defines one or more printable items. If a COLUMN clause is not specified, the items are not printed.

rows.subject: COLUMN clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: printable-size = columns for the characters the PICTURE describes, or, with no PICTURE, the VALUE literal; one column per alphanumeric character (cite.py --check 13.18.14.4 'in the absence of a PICTURE clause, the literal specified in the VALUE clause' -> OK 3)). The emitter advances the horizontal counter by PrintItem.DisplayTextWidth. Probe p5.cob (2023) with each item followed by a relative '|': PIC 9(3)V99 -> 5 columns ('01234', V occupies none), PIC S999 SIGN LEADING SEPARATE -> 4 ('-012'), PIC -ZZ9.99 -> 7 ('- 12.34'), PIC S999 (embedded sign) -> 3, PIC N(2) -> 2: output '01234|-012|- 12.34|01K|AB|' - every boundary exact. Probe p1.cob: `COLUMN 3 VALUE "ABC"` (no PICTURE) occupied 3-5 and `COLUMN PLUS 2` then landed at 7. NOTE 1 is informative. No spec-derived golden isolates printable-size; test-needed. || Code sites (adjudicator detail): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/DataItem.cs#DisplayTextWidth; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/ReportWriterEmitter.cs#EmitFieldPlacements; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Reports.cs (line-width loop ~2690)
rows.rule-text: The printable‑size of a printable item is the number of columns required for printing the characters described by the item's PICTURE clause or, in the absence of a PICTURE clause, the literal specified in the VALUE clause. There is a one‑to‑one correspondence between a column and a character in an alphanumeric character set. NOTE 1 Columns might not line up in a report if the printable characters are not of fixed size encoding, such as UTF-8.

rows.subject: COLUMN clause
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'If an entry containing a LINE clause has no subordinate entry defining a printable item, the resultant report line will be blank.' (cite.py --check 13.18.14.4 -> OK 11)). A LINE with no fields composes the space-filled buffer and returns it. Probe p1.cob (2002): `02 LINE PLUS 1.` with no subordinates between two printing lines produced an empty (blank) record in its position. Also a LINE whose only subordinate lacks COLUMN (p1 line 3 before QQ) prints nothing from it. No spec-derived golden pins a printable-less LINE; test-needed.
rows.rule-text: If an entry containing a LINE clause has no subordinate entry defining a printable item, the resultant report line will be blank.
